feature: Canonical schedule calendar reasons and bounded dependency lead or lag

flows.name: Edit a named project-calendar exception
steps: Edit or add its optional reason
flows.expectedOutcome: The exception date, working status, and optional reason are returned by the API and prefilled on edit

flows.name: Create or edit dependency lead time
steps: Choose a predecessor and relationship type
Enter a negative whole-number lead within the one-year bound
flows.expectedOutcome: The negative value persists as lag_days, is labeled as lead, and affects all four relationship calculations

flows.name: Reconcile duplicate calendar objects safely
steps: Confirm duplicate tables contain no rows
Read back canonical row counts, duplicate object absence, and migration ledger status
flows.expectedOutcome: Canonical calendar data is unchanged and the empty duplicate tables and RPC are removed

flows.name: Fail closed on unavailable calendar or unauthorized dependency writes
steps: Reject anonymous dependency table access and scope authenticated access to project membership
Enforce dependency lag and cycle invariants in the database
Simulate a calendar load or save rejection
Keep calendar editing disabled until a successful retry and preserve the open dialog on save rejection
flows.expectedOutcome: Direct dependency bypasses fail and calendar failures cannot overwrite the saved configuration with a fallback

checks: Calendar reason input remains labeled and usable in the responsive dialog grid
Lead or lag helper text and validation are visible and actionable
No new raw controls bypass the design system

claims.description: Named calendar exceptions round-trip through the canonical API and reopen with their reason
Create and edit accept -365 through 365 while all four relationship types calculate negative lead
Cleanup fails on duplicate data and preserves the canonical calendar row
Project-scoped dependency RLS and database invariants prevent direct bypasses while calendar errors fail closed
The calendar reason and lead or lag controls use labeled design-system components with responsive layout
